stem:
You have a developer device named Device1 that runs macOS and has Homebrew installed.
Device1 will be used by a developer who has a GitHub Copilot plan.
You have a GitHub Enterprise Cloud enterprise account that has data residency at contoso.ghe.com.
You need to install the GitHub Copilot CLI on Device1 and start interactive authentication against the correct GitHub host.
Which two commands should you run in sequence?

options.A: brew install --cask copilot-cli # copilot login --host https://contoso.ghe.com
options.B: brew install copilot-cli # gh auth login --hostname contoso.ghe.com
options.C: brew install --cask copilot-cli # copilot login --host https://github.com
options.D: npm install -g @github/copilot # gh auth login --hostname github.com

explanation:
Current GitHub Copilot documentation uses the standalone Copilot CLI installation and authentication flow.
On macOS with Homebrew, GitHub documents brew install --cask copilot-cli. For a GitHub Enterprise Cloud account with data residency, the CLI should authenticate directly against the enterprise host by using copilot login --host https://SUBDOMAIN.ghe.com; in this scenario that host is https://contoso.ghe.com. This is important because the Copilot license and authentication context must correspond to the GHE.com account that provides access. The PDF's selected commands reflect an older CLI flow and contain OCR or typing errors. For current GitHub Copilot Docs, the verified sequence is the Homebrew cask installation followed by copilot login --host https://contoso.ghe.com.

cat: Configure privacy, content exclusions, and safeguards
stem:
You have a GitHub repository named Repo1 that has GitHub Copilot enabled.
The developers at your company use Repo1 in Microsoft Visual Studio Code.
You need to identify potentially unoriginal suggestions and prevent secrets from being committed to Repo1.
The solution must ensure that the developers can use inline GitHub Copilot suggestions in Visual Studio Code.
Which two actions should you perform? Each correct answer presents part of the solution.

options.A: Enable push protection for secret scanning on Repo1.
options.B: Enable code referencing for GitHub Copilot completions.
options.C: Disable inline GitHub Copilot suggestions in the IDE.
options.D: Add repository custom instructions for secure coding, or create a custom push policy and configure a code check run.

explanation: Two separate GitHub features satisfy the security requirements. Push protection is part of secret scanning and blocks supported secrets before they are pushed to a repository, helping prevent credentials from being committed. GitHub Copilot code referencing addresses potentially unoriginal suggestions: when public-code matches are allowed, accepted inline suggestions that match public GitHub code can be logged with source URLs and license information so developers can review the origin. Disabling inline suggestions would violate the requirement that developers continue using Copilot completions. Repository custom instructions may influence generated code, but they do not replace secret scanning or public-code matching. Therefore, enabling push protection together with Copilot code referencing is the correct combination.
